decision_text: The native fold is NOT admitted as the production default. The binding ground is the bitwise law: the N00 bit battery measured the substitution domain EMPTY (72-point map, 64 rows with ULP divergence, no class rule; the delivered numba fastmath lowering is compiler-context output), and parity is mandatory per una_legacy/madina_legacy/corrected_v1 - so no measured speed can admit the substitution. The measured ROI ground agrees: even a ~4.9x faster fold on the whole replay+splits region saves ~2.40s of the 66.53s run service demand (~3.6%), moving the perfect-packing floor from 16.63s to ~16.03s - still ~1.74x above the 9.21141s sensitivity anchor, i.e. no full-region benefit toward the 10x public gate. The measured comparison is RECORDED, not assumed; the default (delivered numba backend) is rejected for the native route, and the native fold keeps its battery/qualification-only role.

Substantive native support is real code, not a stub; admission waits on a domain where the bitwise law and measured full-region benefit both hold (none measured).
